license_note: The zai-org/GLM-5.3 repository ships a real license file granting use, copying, modification, distribution, deployment, and fine-tuning, but requires any licensee operating a model-as-a-service business above 10 billion US dollars in aggregate affiliate revenue over any consecutive twelve months to pass a Z.AI security review before any commercial use. That gate breaks from the MIT posture of GLM-5, so the release is source-available rather than open source. The Z.ai API is governed separately by platform terms.

license_evidence.scope: zai-org/GLM-5.3 model weights, parameters, configuration files, inference and training code, and associated documentation; does not cover the hosted glm-5.3 API service

access_boundary: This record represents the zai-org/GLM-5.3 FP8 instruction release. The BF16 sibling repository, GLM-5, GLM-5.1, GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3-Flash and its BF16 sibling, Turbo records, the GLM-4.x family, the Z.ai API and chat products, ModelScope mirrors, and downstream quantizations and fine-tunes remain separate boundaries.
strengths: Developer-published 141-shard FP8 checkpoint plus BF16 sibling, tokenizer, and chat template, with documented SGLang, vLLM, TokenSpeed, Transformers, and KTransformers serving paths
First-party Z.ai API documentation names glm-5.3 as a served model with 1M context
tradeoffs: The custom GLM-5.3 License gates commercial use by large model-as-a-service operators behind a Z.AI security review, unlike the MIT posture of GLM-5
Neither the model card nor the API documentation states a versioning policy or deprecation posture
